summary:
Martian Map is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform designed to support scientific analysis and preliminary surface exploration. It integrates three major planetary datasets: MOLA Digital Elevation Models (DEM) for elevation and terrain analysis, Context Camera (CTX) imagery for high-resolution surface observation, and NASA/PSI SWIM 2.0 data for subsurface water-ice consistency mapping across three depth ranges: 0–1 m, 1–5 m, and greater than 5 m.

The platform combines an interactive 2D map using Leaflet with a 3D Mars globe using CesiumJS. Its Python FastAPI backend, powered by Rasterio and NumPy, processes geospatial data and provides elevation queries, terrain analysis, scientific overlays, location intelligence, and waypoint-based route planning.

By bringing scattered planetary datasets into one accessible interface, Martian Map helps researchers and mission planners explore terrain, investigate potential subsurface ice resources, compare locations, and evaluate possible exploration routes. It aims to support more informed, data-driven Mars mission planning while providing preliminary scientific screening rather than certified landing safety or confirmed water discovery.
details:
Martian Map is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform that integrates planetary scientific datasets into a unified 2D and 3D environment.

The platform uses three major datasets: MOLA Digital Elevation Models (DEM) for elevation and terrain analysis, Context Camera (CTX) imagery for detailed surface observation, and NASA/PSI SWIM 2.0 data for mapping subsurface water-ice evidence across three depth ranges: 0–1 m, 1–5 m, and greater than 5 m.

Users can explore Mars through an interactive 2D map powered by Leaflet and a 3D globe powered by CesiumJS. The platform also provides location intelligence, including coordinates, elevation, regional slope and SWIM consistency values. Its waypoint-based route planner evaluates terrain profiles and supports preliminary surface-traverse planning. Additional capabilities include scientific map overlays, geological features, rover tracks, mission scenarios and astronaut suit-resource simulations.

The backend is developed using Python and FastAPI, with Rasterio, NumPy and Pillow for geospatial data processing and tile generation. The frontend uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Three.js for 3D visual elements.

Martian Map addresses the challenge of fragmented planetary data by bringing different scientific sources into one accessible interface. It supports researchers and mission planners in comparing locations, investigating potential ice resources and evaluating exploration routes. The project is designed for preliminary scientific screening and decision support, not certified landing-site safety assessment.
